newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-TENDULKAR BLUNTS WEST INDIAN PACE THREAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR BLUNTS WEST INDIAN PACE THREAT.

text.p: A glorious unbeaten 60 from Sachin Tendulkar frustrated the West Indian pace attack's attempts to blow away India on the second day of the third test at Kensington Oval on Saturday.

Tendulkar lit up the afternoon session with some dazzling strokes to guide his side to 132 for two at the interval in reply to West Indies' 298 all out, a far healthier position than seemed possible when he arrived at the crease.
India had just lost opener Navjot Sidhu for 26 to the first ball he received after lunch on a pitch providing some encouragement to the faster bowlers.

But Tendulkar turned the tide after weathering some high-class bowling from Ian Bishop and Curtly Ambrose, who had earlier removed V.V. Laxman for six, punishing the less experienced Mervyn Dillon whose first three overs cost 33 runs.

In company with the determined Rahul Dravid, who was unbeaten on 24 after more than two hours at tea, the Indian captain put on an unbroken 90 for the third wicket, hitting nine boundaries in a high-class fifty which he reached in 75 balls.
He then celebrated by hooking Franklyn Rose over square leg for six, followed by an exquisite back foot drive to the extra-cover boundary.
Resuming on 240 for seven after Friday's rest day, West Indies earlier added an additional 58 runs in 65 minutes in the morning.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul scored 35 of them to reeach a test-best unbeaten 137 including 13 fours. Venkatesh Prasad trapped last man Dillon lbw for a duck to return figures of five for 82 in 31.4 overs.
